content:
After a hospital stay, arthritis and frailty can make getting home and managing day-to-day harder.

This guide explains discharge planning and what to ask. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

What discharge planning covers

  • When you are likely to go home.
  • Medicines and how to take them.
  • Equipment, such as walking aids or toilet frames.
  • Care and support at home.
  • Follow-up appointments.

Questions to ask

  • Who is my main contact on the ward?
  • What medicines have changed, and why?
  • What equipment will I have?
  • Will I have reablement or physiotherapy at home?
  • Who do I contact if things go wrong?

Reablement and intermediate care

Short-term support can help you regain skills and confidence at home. NICE guidance covers intermediate care and reablement.

Carers

Tell staff if you have a carer, and make sure they are involved. Carers can ask for a carer's assessment.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

Can I refuse to be discharged?

Talk to staff if you are worried about going home. Ask for your concerns to be recorded.

Will equipment be ready?

Ask staff to confirm before you leave.

If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
